transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-17
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sam Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendes (Novus CTO), Aisha Khan (Lead ML Eng), Ben Foster (Infra), Maya Liu (Security)

[00:00] Sam Lee: All right, everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in, hope you all had a good week. I think this is our fourth weekly sync for the VPC pilot, is that right?
[00:07] Carlos Mendes: Yup, fourth. morning for us, afternoon for you.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi all. I put the quick agenda in the chat — network clarifications, driver/AMI mismatch updates, perf numbers, next steps.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. we had some new numbers overnight, so I'll go through those when it's time.

Summary/Recap: 
[02:05] Sam Lee: Quick recap from last week: tunnel established to the private control plane, handshake worked, initial benchmarking ran. Priya, you pushed a model run that hit about p95 210ms, p99 680ms on the r5-like instance class?
[02:22] Priya Nair: Mm yes, that was on the m-instances, the one we noted as m-l8x, sorry the naming in my notes is messy. The main thing was we saw a KV cache cold start penalty — the first 20 requests had higher latencies until cache warmed. After warmup, steady-state p95 dropped to around 160ms.
[02:40] Ben Foster: We also saw some dropped connections on the control-plane side when we had a node restart, that might be related to our NAT gateway rules.

Network discussion:
[05:10] Carlos Mendes: On the networking front, Maya's team is worried about egress IPs — we need static egress IPs whitelisted for our firewall vendor, plus we need to keep audit logs internal. We thought using a NAT Gateway would be simplest, but there was a suggestion for egress-only VPC endpoints, which avoid NAT egress charges.
[05:32] Maya Liu: Right, from a security posture we prefer predictable IPs. NAT with Elastic IP works, but pricing is a thing. Also we want control-plane comms to go over the peered VPC — is the control-plane traffic using a private peering or going via public egress?
[05:49] Priya Nair: Currently pilot uses a secure peering connection to Redwood's control plane in our staging region, but the data plane for model packets is routed out through your VPC egress. We can support private link/proxy if you prefer — there's a prebuilt option for private provisioning. I should note there's some mislabeling in our internal docs — we called it VPC peering but it's actually a managed private link in this setup.
[06:12] Ben Foster: Ah, ok that explains mismatch with our security doc. can you share the network diagram?
[06:20] Priya Nair: Yes, I'll re-share updated topology (link: https://redwood.ai/pilot/diagrams) and add route table snapshots.

Route tables and NAT specifics:
[08:40] Ben Foster: We saw a route that points 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT, and a specific route for the control plane CIDR to the peering. But during the node restart the health-check IP was not reachable because the subnet ACLs are a bit restrictive. I can send screenshots.
[09:01] Sam Lee: Thanks, Ben. Action — Ben to confirm NAT Gateway vs. egress-only endpoint and share route table screenshots.

Driver/AMI and node upgrade discussion:
[11:30] Aisha Khan: On perf, our infra team discovered the pilot nodes are running an AMI with CUDA 11.3 but our benchmarking AMI from your docs uses CUDA 11.8, so there's a mismatch on the cuDNN binaries. That caused some lower throughput and occasional timeout on one of the GPU pods.
[11:48] Priya Nair: Right, that was one of the things we flagged in the last deep-dive. The runtime picks kernels depending on the driver — if drivers are older, certain fused kernels are unavailable and we fall back to slower ops which spike p99.
[12:05] Carlos Mendes: Is it risky to upgrade nodes in pilot? We have a tight maintenance window.
[12:12] Priya Nair: It's standard infra work but we recommend a rolling upgrade — upgrade a small batch, validate throughput, then continue. We can help with an AMI recipe so you get the recommended CUDA/CUDNN plus kernel compatible packages.
[12:24] Sam Lee: Priya will provide the exact CUDA/CUDNN matrix and recommended AMI, action item noted.

Performance numbers and KV cache warmup:
[15:00] Aisha Khan: The overnight run: 100k synthetic requests, 3 models — the main trimmed model averaged tokens/sec 18. p95 after warmup 150ms, p99 around 650ms. KV cache warmup caused first 500 requests to be slow where p95 was closer to 480ms initially. We're looking to reduce that via pre-warm strategy.
[15:25] Priya Nair: We saw similar; pre-populating the KV cache with prefix requests reduced the cold-start tail by ~30%. Also batching settings are important — set max batch wait to 8ms and max batch size to 16 for this workload.
[15:40] Aisha Khan: We'll test your batching recommendations. Also curious about autoscale behavior — how does Redwood Dedicated behave in private setup?
[15:50] Priya Nair: In Private we support both autoscaling via a controller and static pools. For pilot we'd recommend static scale-up to avoid unexpected node churn while we tune. Once stable, enable autoscale with conservative cooldowns.

Security/compliance questions:
[19:05] Maya Liu: Quick question on KMS — does Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS keys for model encryption at rest and for signing audit logs? Need to confirm key rotation cadence and HSM usage.
[19:20] Priya Nair: Yes, we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles. We support customer-managed keys and rotation — we'll send the KMS integration guide. For high-compliance we can plug in HSM-backed keys but that path has additional setup time.
[19:35] Maya Liu: Also, audit logs retention — we need 12 months. Can you store them in our S3 bucket?
[19:42] Jorge Alvarez: Yes, logs can be exported to your S3, and retention/prefix can be configured; we'll include the doc.

Benchmarks and regression:
[23:10] Aisha Khan: There was one regression when we switched instance class — throughput dipped by 8% at one point, I think due to an older driver fallback. After rolling back it improved. We're going to run another 100k with driver updates.
[23:28] Priya Nair: If you share the raw benchmark CSV I'll parse it and send a short analysis sheet. Small note: some model names were transcribed incorrectly in our logs — "redwood-ggml" shows as "redwood-gml" in the exported CSV; ignore that.
[23:45] Sam Lee: Action: Priya to send trimmed benchmark results and p95/p99 tails.

Operational notes & fallbacks:
[27:00] Ben Foster: If we hit capacity issues in the private pool, is there an automatic fallback to hosted Redwood models, or do requests fail?
[27:11] Priya Nair: We support a fallback policy — you can set automatic routing to a compatible hosted variant in the same API surface. There are auth and egress considerations — we can show a canary policy that first tries private then falls back with a degrade flag.
[27:28] Carlos Mendes: Important for us: we need tokens to never leave region X unless encrypted and approved. Is fallback to hosted allowed if traffic leaves region?
[27:38] Sam Lee: We'll update the policy doc. By default fallback is opt-in; we'll not enable it for your pilot unless you sign off.

Scheduling an upgrade window:
[31:10] Sam Lee: Proposed upgrade window to align CUDA/driver: 2027-06-24 morning (PT). Who needs to be involved?
[31:20] Ben Foster: Our infra leads can do that date but need 48h notice.
[31:25] Maya Liu: Security needs to review the upgrade AMI.
[31:28] Aisha Khan: We can run a canary set the evening before.
[31:33] Sam Lee: Okay, tentatively set 2027-06-24. Ben to confirm route table screenshots by 2027-06-19. Priya to provide AMI matrix by 2027-06-18.

Open questions and risks:
[34:50] Carlos Mendes: Two risks: 1) if KV cache warmup remains high we can't meet p95 targets for user-facing inference; 2) network egress/dns timeouts during node restarts cause transient errors — we need retry logic.
[35:05] Priya Nair: For (1) we recommend cache prefill and small warm pools; for (2) implement client retry with idempotency and we'll adjust health-check timings to reduce churn. We'll share a retry pattern snippet in the runbook.

Recap and next steps:
[38:40] Sam Lee: Quick recap: Ben to share route table screenshots and confirm NAT vs egress-only endpoint, Aisha to run second 100k synth load and share raw CSV, Priya to send AMI/driver matrix and parse bench results, Sam will send pricing note and runbook update. Tentative upgrade window 2027-06-24.
[39:02] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. will loop in our infra on the calendar.
[39:08] Maya Liu: We'll validate egress IP whitelist.

[41:20] Sam Lee: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the thread with docs and action items. meeting adjourned.

References and shared artifacts:
- Pilot network diagram (updated): https://redwood.ai/pilot/diagrams
- Benchmark CSV (uploaded to pilot folder) - note: model name transcription issues
- KMS integration doc (will be sent)
- Runbook draft (link to be shared by Sam)

End of transcript.
